html:
No'iria is the name the map gives a small territory in the Beni lowlands of northern Bolivia, near the Beni and Mamoré rivers. Standard sources say little about a people by this name.

The peoples of this area, such as the Panoan-speaking Chácobo and their neighbours, lived by farming manioc and maize in forest clearings, fishing and hunting. The region was hit hard by Jesuit and later Bolivian settlement and above all by the rubber boom of the late 1800s, which forced many people into labour on the rivers. See also the wider Amazon peoples.
